title: A Harbor for the Songbook
premise: Ada Kavanagh has built her career ghostwriting other people's truths, including the memoir of her rival, publishing magnate Vivian Marsh — a book that will bury the man Ada once loved with a decade of letters she never sent. When Cormac Bell, the letter-writer himself, moves in next door and begins recognizing his own words surfacing in Vivian's advance chapters, Ada must decide whether to protect the career that saved her from ruin or help Cormac reclaim the story that was stolen from him. As Vivian's lawyers close in and Ada's authorship of the betrayal comes to light, she chooses confession over survival, testifying to Cormac's authorship at the cost of her own name. The book ends with Ada publishing her first novel under her own hand, and Cormac — having forgiven but not forgotten — standing in her doorway with a new letter, this one addressed to her.
about_author: Isandro Galloway is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing unsent correspondence before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal town where he claims every neighbor has a story they'd rather he didn't tell.

chapters.title: The Unsent Decade
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet Ada mid-ghostwrite, drafting Vivian Marsh's memoir in a borrowed voice while her own novel sits unfinished in a drawer. A courier delivers a box of old letters she recognizes instantly — Cormac's handwriting, ten years of them, which she secretly transcribed for Vivian. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into complicity; Ada realizes she is not just witness to the theft but its instrument.

chapters.title: The Man Next Door
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. Cormac Bell moves into the neighboring unit of Ada's building, unknowing and unguarded, carrying grief and a habit of writing letters no one answers. He and Ada collide over a broken elevator and a shared umbrella. Emotional beat: warmth arriving at the worst possible time; the reader feels the trap closing before either character does.

chapters.title: Borrowed Voices
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ada and Cormac grow close through small domestic rituals while she continues feeding Vivian's manuscript. Cormac mentions a memoir deal he lost years ago and reads an advance excerpt online — and freezes at a sentence only he ever wrote. Emotional beat: recognition as vertigo; intimacy curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: What Vivian Keeps
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Inside Marsh House: Vivian's rationale for the theft, her failing health, her hunger to be remembered as more than a publisher of other people's genius. She summons Ada, praises her discretion, and hints she knows about the letters' true origin. Emotional beat: power shown as seduction; Ada understands Vivian could destroy her with one phone call.

chapters.title: Second Drafts
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. Cormac investigates the excerpt, tracing it to Ada's literary agency, and confronts her gently, giving her room to lie. She lies badly. He leaves without accusation, which wounds worse than anger. Emotional beat: the price of survival made personal; Ada watches trust die in real time and does nothing to stop it.

chapters.title: The Kill Fee
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Vivian offers Ada co-authorship and a fortune to finish the book fast, contingent on signing an NDA that erases Cormac entirely. Ada's debts, her mother's care costs, her whole rescued life hang on the signature. Emotional beat: temptation rendered honestly; the reader wants her to sign even while dreading it.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. Cormac finds the original letters Ada returned to him years ago — pages subtly annotated in her hand, proof she was the conduit all along. Instead of rage, he reads them aloud alone, grieving the decade and the woman both. Emotional beat: sorrow deeper than betrayal; love revealed as the thing that makes the wound possible.

chapters.title: The Advance Copy
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The finished memoir ships to reviewers. Ada holds her own nameless contribution in print and breaks — she sends Cormac the full draft, her confession attached, then walks into Vivian's office and resigns, naming herself as ghostwriter of the stolen chapters. Emotional beat: climax of choice; ruin embraced deliberately, hands shaking, spine straight.

chapters.title: Marsh House Falls
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cormac goes public with provenance evidence; Vivian's empire fractures under scandal and her own illness, and she dies before the retraction prints, leaving Ada a final letter that is neither apology nor forgiveness — only acknowledgment. Emotional beat: victory that tastes like ash; power's corruption outlived by the people it used.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Songbook
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, coda. Months later, Ada publishes her first novel under her own name to modest notice, and Cormac appears at her door holding a single new letter — addressed to her, sealed, offered freely. She doesn't open it yet; some things should be read slowly. Emotional beat: earned tenderness; second chances finally arriving on time.
